beats.text: Why may no boat come within three miles of this island?
Who is the ban protecting, them or us?
It's home to the Sentinelese, an uncontacted tribe.
From orbit, I keep an eye on it safely.
That forbidden ring of sea dwarfs the island itself.
A nineteen fifty-six regulation bans visits, and the Indian Navy patrols.
It shields the islanders from mainland diseases they likely have no immunity to.
If an outsider lands and is killed, India won't prosecute the islanders.
Next target: an island born in nineteen sixty-three. Follow for the next scan. Orbi out.

draft.description: North Sentinel Island in India's Andaman Islands is home to the Sentinelese, an uncontacted indigenous tribe. A 1956 regulation bans travel there and any approach closer than five kilometers, to protect them from mainland infectious diseases.
